next_state_election.name: General Election
next_state_election.source_name: Illinois State Board of Elections — 2026 General Election

glance_notes.source_name: Illinois State Board of Elections — Register to Vote on Election Day
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration: Illinois provides several registration options. Regular registration closes 28 days before the election, online voter registration remains available through the 16th day before the election, and Grace Period Registration allows eligible voters to register or update their registration and vote after the regular deadline through Election Day.

glance_notes.source_name: Illinois State Board of Elections — Voting by Mail
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Vote by Mail: Any registered Illinois voter may vote by mail without providing an excuse. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the first day to apply was August 5 and mailed or online requests must be received by the election authority by October 29.

glance_notes.source_name: Illinois State Board of Elections — Register to Vote on Election Day
glance_notes.text: Election Day Registration: Illinois allows eligible residents to register and vote on Election Day at designated Grace Period registration and voting locations. A person registering on Election Day must provide two forms of identification, with at least one showing the current registration address.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Illinois residents can register online through the Illinois State Board of Elections, by mail, in person through an election authority or qualified deputy registrar, through participating government agencies, or through Grace Period Registration after the regular registration deadline. To register, you must be a U.S. citizen, be at least 18 years old by the applicable General or Consolidated Election, and have lived in your election precinct for at least 30 days before Election Day. Illinois also permits qualified 17-year-olds to register and vote in a primary if they will be 18 by the following General Election. A person currently serving a sentence of confinement for a criminal conviction is not eligible to vote, but voting eligibility is restored after release from confinement.
register.glance_value: Online, mail, in person or Grace Period registration
register.source_name: Illinois State Board of Elections — Voter Registration and Voting
register.internal_note: The Illinois State Board of Elections voter resources provide online and paper registration, automatic voter registration, deputy registrar information and Grace Period Registration. The Board's 2026 voter materials separately address voting eligibility for people with past convictions or awaiting trial. Eligibility following criminal conviction depends on whether the individual is currently serving confinement rather than permanently losing voting rights.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use the Illinois State Board of Elections Registration and Polling Place Lookup to check whether you are registered and find your Election Day polling place. If your registration information is missing or incorrect, contact your local election authority. Illinois elections are administered locally by county clerks and boards of election commissioners.
check_registration.glance_value: Use the state registration and polling-place lookup
check_registration.source_name: Illinois State Board of Elections — Registration and Voting
check_registration.internal_note: The State Board's official voter-information portal provides both an 'Am I Registered to Vote in Illinois?' service and a Registration/Polling Place Lookup. Local election authorities maintain and administer voter registration records.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: For the November 3, 2026 General Election, regular voter registration closes October 6, 2026. Illinois online voter registration remains available through October 18. Eligible residents who miss those deadlines may use Grace Period Registration to register or update their registration and vote through Election Day. Election Day registrants must appear at a designated Grace Period registration and voting location and provide two forms of identification, at least one showing the current registration address.
deadlines.glance_value: Regular deadline October 6; online through October 18; Grace Period afterward
deadlines.source_name: Illinois State Board of Elections — Register to Vote on Election Day
deadlines.internal_note: Illinois closes regular registration 28 days before an election under the Election Code, making October 6 the regular deadline for the November 3, 2026 General Election. Online registration continues through the 16th day before the election, October 18. Grace Period Registration continues after regular registration closes and through Election Day. Chicago and Cook County voters should also follow instructions from their applicable local election authority.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Illinois voters may use the State Board of Elections Registration and Polling Place Lookup to find their designated Election Day polling place. On Election Day, a voter may cast a ballot at the designated polling place or at an Election Day Vote Center if the voter's election authority operates one. Early-voting and Grace Period locations are separate and are published by local election authorities.
polling_place.source_name: Illinois State Board of Elections — Election Day Voting
polling_place.internal_note: The official Election Day Voting page directly states that voters may vote at their designated polling place or at a vote center designated by their election authority and provides the polling-place and registration lookup tool. Vote-center availability varies by jurisdiction.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: For the November 3, 2026 General Election, Illinois polling places are open from 6:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m. Voters may cast a ballot at their designated polling place or at an Election Day Vote Center when their election authority provides one. Eligible residents who still need to register or update their registration may use a designated Grace Period registration and voting location. A voter whose name does not appear on the official voter list or whose eligibility is challenged may be entitled to cast a provisional ballot.
election_day.source_name: Illinois State Board of Elections — Election Day Voting
election_day.internal_note: The current State Board Election Day Voting page directly establishes 6:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. hours, designated polling places, jurisdiction-specific Election Day Vote Centers and provisional voting. Election Day registration requirements are separately established at [https://www.elections.il.gov/ElectionOperations/RegisterToVoteOnElectionDay.aspx](https://www.elections.il.gov/ElectionOperations/RegisterToVoteOnElectionDay.aspx).

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: Illinois polling places are open from 6:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m. on Election Day. A voter who is in line when the polls close at 7:00 p.m. is entitled to remain and vote.
polling_hours.source_name: Illinois State Board of Elections — Election Day Voting
polling_hours.internal_note: The Illinois State Board of Elections directly states that polling places are open from 6:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. Illinois Election Code §§ 17-1 and 18-2 independently establish the same statewide hours: [https://ilga.gov/legislation/ILCS/details?ActID=170&ActName=Election+Code.&ChapAct=10+ILCS+5%2F&Chapter=ELECTIONS&ChapterID=3&MajorTopic=GOVERNMENT](https://ilga.gov/legislation/ILCS/details?ActID=170&ActName=Election+Code.&ChapAct=10+ILCS+5%2F&Chapter=ELECTIONS&ChapterID=3&MajorTopic=GOVERNMENT).

early_voting.label: Early Voting
early_voting.content: Illinois provides in-person early voting before Election Day. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, early voting begins at designated election-authority locations on September 24 and continues through November 2. Additional early-voting sites and schedules are established by local election authorities. Voters using early voting do not need to provide a reason or excuse. Grace Period Registration and voting are also available during the applicable period at designated locations.
early_voting.source_name: Illinois State Board of Elections — Early Voting Information
early_voting.internal_note: Under Illinois Election Code Article 19A, early voting for a general election begins on the 40th day before Election Day, which is September 24, 2026, and continues through the day before Election Day, November 2. Local election authorities establish additional early-voting locations and operating hours. The State Board provides an Early Voting/Grace Period Registration/Election Day Vote Center location service. Because locations and daily hours vary by jurisdiction, voters should use the live local information.

absentee_mail.label: Vote by Mail
absentee_mail.content: Any registered Illinois voter may vote by mail without providing an excuse. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, voters could begin applying for a vote-by-mail ballot on August 5. Applications submitted by mail or through an authorized remote request process must be received by the election authority by October 29. Voters may also apply in person under the deadlines established by Illinois law. A returned vote-by-mail ballot must be postmarked by Election Day and received by the election authority within 14 days after Election Day to be counted. Illinois also allows voters to apply for permanent vote-by-mail status so that ballots are automatically sent for elections for which they are eligible.
absentee_mail.glance_value: No excuse; mail request deadline October 29
absentee_mail.source_name: Illinois State Board of Elections — Voting by Mail
absentee_mail.internal_note: The current State Board page directly identifies November 3, 2026 as the next election, August 5 as the first application date, October 29 as the deadline for requests by mail, and November 2 as the final day of early voting. Illinois Election Code Article 19 provides the timely-postmark and 14-day receipt rule. The State Board's 2026 Illinois Voter Guide for Voting by Mail provides current permanent vote-by-mail guidance. UOCAVA voters have separate procedures documented in military_overseas.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Illinois does not generally require an already-registered voter to present photo identification simply to cast a regular ballot. Identification may be required in specific circumstances, including certain first-time voters whose identity was not previously verified and people registering or updating a registration through Grace Period Registration. A person registering on Election Day must provide two forms of identification, at least one of which shows the current registration address. Acceptable documents can include a driver's license, Social Security card, utility bill, employee or student identification card, residential lease or contract, credit card, civic or professional membership card, or FOID card.
voter_id.glance_value: No general photo-ID requirement for registered voters
voter_id.source_name: Illinois State Board of Elections — Election Day Registration
voter_id.internal_note: Illinois does not impose a general photo-ID requirement on an already registered voter casting a regular ballot. The State Board's Election Day registration page directly establishes the two-document requirement for same-day registrants and provides examples of acceptable documents. Federal HAVA identification requirements can apply to certain first-time voters who registered by mail without providing verified identifying information. These circumstances should not be presented as a statewide photo-ID requirement.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Illinois provides accessible voting options for voters with disabilities. Election jurisdictions use voting systems tested and certified for use in Illinois, and voters are entitled to instruction on the voting equipment. Voters with disabilities may receive assistance from election judges or, subject to legal restrictions, from a person of their choice. Illinois also provides an Accessible Vote by Mail program for voters with print disabilities, allowing eligible voters to receive a ballot electronically and mark and verify it using their own assistive technology.
accessible_voting.source_name: Illinois State Board of Elections — Accessible Vote by Mail
accessible_voting.internal_note: The State Board's current Voting by Mail page directly establishes electronic ballot delivery for voters with print disabilities and use of personal assistive technology. Election Day Voting — [https://www.elections.il.gov/ElectionOperations/ElectionDayVoting.aspx](https://www.elections.il.gov/ElectionOperations/ElectionDayVoting.aspx) — confirms instruction on voting systems and assistance for voters with disabilities. The State Board also publishes a dedicated 2026 Illinois Voter Guide for voters with disabilities.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Illinois provides special registration and vote-by-mail procedures for members of the U.S. uniformed services, eligible family members and qualified U.S. citizens living overseas. Eligible voters may use the Federal Post Card Application to register and request a vote-by-mail ballot. Illinois also operates electronic systems that allow covered voters to communicate with local election officials and obtain election materials. Depending on the voter's Illinois jurisdiction, the voter may use the state's MOVE system or an authorized OmniBallot system. A federal or state write-in ballot may be available when the regular ballot has not arrived in time.
military_overseas.glance_value: FPCA, MOVE/OmniBallot and write-in options available
military_overseas.source_name: Illinois State Board of Elections — Military and Overseas Voting
military_overseas.internal_note: The current State Board page establishes UOCAVA eligibility, simultaneous registration and ballot requests for military personnel, FPCA use and Illinois MOVE. It states that UOCAVA voters in the City of Chicago, Cook County, DuPage County, Lake County, Marshall County and Sangamon County instead use the authorized OmniBallot system. The Board also publishes a 2026 Illinois Voter Guide for Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voters. Because procedures vary by voter category and jurisdiction, the reader-facing section avoids applying ordinary domestic vote-by-mail deadlines to UOCAVA voters.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: College students may register in Illinois if they meet the state's voter eligibility and residence requirements. A student living at an Illinois college may establish that location as a voting residence when it is the student's permanent abode for voting purposes, or may remain registered at another qualifying residence. A voter can be registered and vote from only one residence. Students registering during the Grace Period may use qualifying documents to establish identity and residence; a student identification card is one of the documents Illinois lists as potentially acceptable, but two forms of identification are required and at least one must show the registration address.
student_voting.glance_value: Students may register where they establish voting residence
student_voting.source_name: Illinois State Board of Elections — 2026 Illinois Voter Guide for College Students
student_voting.internal_note: The State Board currently publishes a dedicated 2026 Illinois Voter Guide for College Students. Election Day registration documentation requirements are independently established at [https://www.elections.il.gov/ElectionOperations/RegisterToVoteOnElectionDay.aspx](https://www.elections.il.gov/ElectionOperations/RegisterToVoteOnElectionDay.aspx). The section deliberately does not claim that attending an Illinois college automatically establishes Illinois voting residence.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Illinois election authorities publish specimen or sample ballots before an election. Because ballot contents depend on the voter's address, districts and local questions, voters should use their local election authority's official ballot information or the Illinois State Board of Elections voter resources to identify the ballot that applies to them. Illinois law requires election authorities to publish specimen ballots before the election.
sample_ballot.glance_value: Available through your local election authority
sample_ballot.source_name: Illinois State Board of Elections — Information for Voters
sample_ballot.internal_note: The Illinois Election Code requires election authorities to publish specimen ballots before elections. The State Board's election calendar specifically includes a statutory specimen-ballot publication deadline. Because Illinois ballots vary substantially by election jurisdiction, precinct and district, the local election authority is the appropriate official source for a voter's actual sample ballot.

contact.content: Illinois State Board of Elections, Springfield Office, 2329 S. MacArthur Blvd., Springfield, IL 62704. Phone: 217-782-4141. Fax: 217-782-5959. TTY: 800-964-3013. Springfield office hours are Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The Chicago Office is at 69 W. Washington, Suite LL08, Chicago, IL 60602. Phone: 312-814-6440. Chicago office hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. General email: webmaster@elections.il.gov. For questions about an individual registration, polling place, early-voting site or vote-by-mail ballot, contact the appropriate local election authority.
contact.source_name: Illinois State Board of Elections — Contact Information
contact.internal_note: The current State Board contact page directly verifies both office addresses, office hours, telephone and fax numbers, TTY number and [webmaster@elections.il.gov](mailto:webmaster@elections.il.gov) for general division questions. The email address is plain text in this JSON and is not wrapped in Markdown or mailto syntax.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the Illinois State Board of Elections website for statewide voter information, online registration, registration and polling-place lookup, vote-by-mail information, election dates, military and overseas voting resources, accessibility guidance and voter guides. Elections are administered locally by county clerks and boards of election commissioners, which provide jurisdiction-specific polling places, early-voting and Grace Period locations, vote centers, ballot drop boxes and sample ballots.
official_resources.glance_value: State Board of Elections & local election authorities
official_resources.internal_note: Official voter information: [https://www.elections.il.gov/InformationForVoters.aspx](https://www.elections.il.gov/InformationForVoters.aspx). Official registration and voting information: [https://www.elections.il.gov/ElectionOperations/RegistrationAndVoting.aspx](https://www.elections.il.gov/ElectionOperations/RegistrationAndVoting.aspx). Official Election Day voting: [https://www.elections.il.gov/ElectionOperations/ElectionDayVoting.aspx](https://www.elections.il.gov/ElectionOperations/ElectionDayVoting.aspx). Official vote-by-mail information: [https://www.elections.il.gov/ElectionOperations/VotingByMail.aspx](https://www.elections.il.gov/ElectionOperations/VotingByMail.aspx). Official military and overseas voting: [https://www.elections.il.gov/VotingAndRegistrationSystems/Military.aspx](https://www.elections.il.gov/VotingAndRegistrationSystems/Military.aspx). Official state contact information: [https://www.elections.il.gov/Main/ContactUs.aspx](https://www.elections.il.gov/Main/ContactUs.aspx). All source_url fields are bare URL strings, and reader-facing content contains no Markdown hyperlink syntax.
